Issued at 413 PM CDT Thu Oct 29 2026

Currently through tonight...

Been an overall quiet day across the area today...though
satellite imagery shows a stark contrast in sky cover from 
north to south. Low-level stratus that started working its way 
into the area late last night has remained stubbornly in place 
over southern half, keeping skies overcast...vs the northern 
half which has had no shortage of sun. Looking aloft, flow 
across the region remains west- southwesterly...with broad 
ridging over much of the southeastern CONUS, while a stronger 
area of low pressure is making its way into the Pac NW region. 
To our south-southwest, satellite imagery showing a shortwave 
disturbance making its way north through the TX/NM/Mex border 
region. The overall surface pattern is on the weaker side...the 
main frontal boundary is draped from WSW-ENE across central KS, 
with weak high pressure centered over the Dakotas. This has kept
winds easterly across the area today, with speeds mainly 10- 
15, with an occasional gust closer to 20 MPH. Western portions 
of north central KS have been struggling to even get to 60 
today, rest of the area has been more in the mid 60s.

This evening and tonight...still have the potential for some  
precipitation to work it way NNE through the region, driven by 
increasing warm air/moisture advection as the low-level jet
ramps up. Models not showing any overly strong LLJ, generally 
around 30kts, and even at this point still showing some 
differences with just how much coverage there ends up being. 
Expecting coverage to be on the scattered side of things...with 
models still focusing the better chances mainly near/east of HWY
281. Can't rule out some of this activity being thunderstorms 
with instability also building back north with time...and a 
stronger storm is not out of the question, but the overall 
threat for severe weather remains low. 

Friday through the weekend...

Some of this activity from tonight may linger across especially 
eastern areas to start off the day on Friday...but most models
show a lull between this round and the next working in later 
in the day. Really hasn't been any significant changes with 
models through Friday, with the main focus being that above 
mentioned upper level disturbance over TX/NM/Mex...which will 
continue trekking northward with time, roughly reaching into srn
KS by evening. Still some differences between models with the 
timing of the main shield of precipitation reaching the southern
edge of the forecast area...could be seeing at least scattered 
activity already by mid-late afternoon, with the better chances 
looking to focus mainly after 00Z into the overnight hours. Some
models are also showing the chance that this system weakens 
slightly as it pushes north through the area...potentially 
diminishing the overall coverage of activity with time. Similar 
to tonight...instability in the area keeps the threat for 
thunderstorms around, but the threat for severe weather remains 
low. Higher dewpoints/better moisture building in will help any 
activity being efficient rain-makers...so any spots that have a 
stronger storm or any training could pick up at least an inch of
rain through Friday night.

Confidence in precipitation chances for the upcoming weekend are
not high...with models difference with the timing of this 
latest system working east of the area and when precip wanes. 
Some models are pretty slow, keeping the potential for at least 
scattered preciptiation around much of/if not all of the day on 
Saturday, a few lingering even longer. Forecast currently has 
much of the day Sunday dry with some weak shortwave ridging 
moving through...but any break would likely be brief, as chances
ramp back up Sunday night. 

As far as temperatures go, not looking at any notable
swings...but with the plentiful precip chances and potential 
cloud cover make for a lower confidence forecast. Expecting 
highs generally in the 60s Fri-Sun...depending on precip timing 
into the daytime hours, some spots may struggle to even get to 
60.

New work week...

Main story Sunday night, and moreso into Monday-
Tuesday...continues to lie with the next upper level storms 
system working onto the Plains. Models remain in generally 
decent agreement big picture-wise with the upper level pattern 
through the weekend...showing the low pressure system currently 
over the Pac NW digging south as it shifts east...by 12Z Monday 
showing the main troughing working through the Rockies. Still 
plenty of differences between models beyond then, with how the 
pattern evolves as the system moves through the Plains...with 
recent runs having trended more toward a messy passage, and 
instead of one solid low, there is the potential for a few 
embedded vort maxes in the overall troughing. Recent trends have
shown the potential for a first push of more widespread 
precipitation late Sunday night into the daytime hours
